LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. The former first-round pick has 78 targets in eight games, reeling in 53 passes for 648 yards and two scores. While he hasn’t found the end zone a bunch in 2026, Nabers has at least six grabs in five of his eight games and has four straight matchups with at least eight targets. He had a huge game against Washington earlier this season, pulling down 11 of his 20 targets for 121 yards and a score. The Commanders have struggled against the pass all season long, ranking 18th in the league in passing yards allowed while also allowing the sixth-most passing scores. I expect Nabers to be heavily involved in the game plan once again on Thursday night. Daniels torched the Giants on the ground in Week 5, rushing nine times for 103 yards and two scores. He has just two games this season with over 35.5 rushing yards, but Daniels has really killed the Giants on the ground in his NFL career. The star quarterback has 44, 35, 68 and 103 rushing yards in his four games against the division rival, and New York has given up the third-most rushing yards to the quarterback position in 2026. A lot of that is because of Daniels’ big game, but I like this matchup for the Commanders signal-caller on Thursday. New York has struggled to get home this season, posting the worst pressure rate in the NFL while picking up just 16 sacks in eight games. Even though the Giants are third in the NFL in success rate, they have shown that they can’t keep contain on Daniels, who is one of the best athletes in open space in the league. Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has been a touchdown machine in the 2026 season, reeling in 46 of his 69 targets for 448 yards and six scores. He’s coming off a score in Week 9 against Philly, and Likely has a couple of multi-score games in 2026. Plus, he’s been a beast when the Giants get near the end zone. In the red zone, Likely has nine targets in 2026, turning those into eight catches and five touchdowns. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. picks.blurb: NFL Betting Advice: Giants-Commanders picks and props - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day NFL Betting Advice: Giants-Commanders picks and props Rematch! | Getty Images David Hartman · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 10 edition! Each week, I'm giving you my three favorite wagers for that week's New York Giants game. My one rule: I won't ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The 5-2-1 Giants host the 2-5-1 Commanders on Thursday Night Football, and it's Big Blue's first rematch of the season. Fans will remember that the first contest between these teams resulted in the NFL's only tie this season, with each team blowing an easy chance to win at the end of overtime. I'm guessing we'll get another close game this time around. Jameis Winston was the Giant's quarterback in that Week 5 contest, but now he's backing up J.J. McCarthy, who gets his third start for New York on Thursday. The Giants are coming off their first win in Philadelphia in 13 years, and they continue to lead a weakened NFC East. It wasn't pretty, but a win is a win. Not only did the Giants break their long losing streak at the Linc, but they also broke a strange streak of scoring 27 points in three straight games, starting with that Week 5 tie with Washington. They scored 19 against the Eagles, and their only touchdown drive was led by Winston, after McCarthy was briefly knocked out of the game. McCarthy is good to go on Thursday and Big Blue should also have Cam Skattebo back. The Commanders fell at home to the Rams last week, 20-13. Jayden Daniels continues to play mistake-free football, but Washington struggled to move the ball and score. For the second straight week, the Giants have an opportunity to effectively put away a division rival for the 2026 season. My picks were 1-2 in Week 9 and I'm 13-11 on the season. I did go 3-0 when these teams met the first time, so I'll try to replicate that this week. Let's get to this week's picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel , as of Wednesday, November 11. The line for the game is Giants -1.5, with a total of 41.5. Daniels ran wild in Week 5 | Getty Images Giants -1.5 (-120) . Looking at the teams' records, and the fact that this game is being played at MetLife Stadium, this line feels surprisingly low. Is it a trap line? Maybe. But throw in that the Giants are coached by John Harbaugh while Dan Quinn is on the other side and I'm jumping on the value. Outside of the quarterback position, it's hard to find a spot where Washington is clearly better. Both teams have dealt with a lot of injuries, but Washington is not only without its top receiver and running back, but now both of its starting defensive tackles (DaRon Payne and Javon Kinlaw) are out. This won't be an easy game for New York by any stretch, but I think they're the better team and will come away with the win. The Giants' moneyline (-135) offers similar value. Jayden Daniels OVER 34.5 rushing yards (-114). This was my favorite prop is Week 5, and it hit big-time, with Daniels rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns. New York will need to do a much better job of trying to contain him this time around, and I'm sure Dennard Wilson has a plan. Maybe Arvell Reese will spy him some? I still think Daniels should easily get to this total. New York's secondary is playing great football, and Daniels won't hesitate to take off when there's nothing there. Malik Nabers longest reception OVER 23.5 yards (-106). I'd really like to take Nabers over 5.5 receptions, but at -134 its not eligible. I'll take this prop. The Commanders have a porous secondary, and they rank 30 th in the league in passing yards allowed per game (240). McCarthy struggled to get Nabers the ball last week but that shouldn't be the case on Thursday. Puka Nacua absolutely demolished Washington last week (14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown, on 19 targets), even though everyone in the building knew he was the first read on most dropbacks. Nabers just needs one big play for this to hit, and I don't think that's a problem. He's had a catch of at least 22 yards in five straight contests. Those are the picks for Week 10. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 10 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, coming soon.

The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying , "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans." Lions vs. Patriots where to watch Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location : Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany) TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Lions -2.5 ( via DraftKings ) Lions vs. Patriots prediction I think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win. This week, they head to Munich, Germany, to play the New England Patriots in a rare above-.500 battle across the pond. Since it's an early kickoff, it's best to get your bets in sooner rather than later, because if you don't have your morning coffee, you could end up placing the wrong bet! Last week was a losing week, as the Lions' defense did their part, but the offense struggled more than I expected. Now two games below .500, we need a perfect 3/3 week to get back above, or at least two out of the three to get back to even. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Jared Goff Over 268.5 passing yards (-112) Lions quarterback Jared Goff is having a solid season so far, and despite a quiet game against the Miami Dolphins last week, I think he will rebound well against New England. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards against the Patriots, the most they've allowed this season. That was at home for New England too; now they are on the road and without their top cornerback, Carlton Davis III. Goff will want to rebound after being held without a passing touchdown for the first time this season last week. With his star wide receiver, Amon-Ra St. Brown, also having ties to Germany, he will do his best to get him a touchdown in front of his home crowd. Goff has thrown for over 268 yards in five games this season, and with New England allowing an average of 231.9 yards per game, going above that by only 37 seems doable with the weapons he has. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 2. Jameson Williams Alt receiving yards 50+ (-158) Piggybacking off the first point with Goff, I think this secondary, without its No. 2 corner Davis, will have its hands full with wide receivers St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Packers' top two receivers got over 100 yards each in last week's win, and each also had at least one catch over 40 yards. Williams is a big-play receiver; he can do that on one play, too. His speed will be tough to contain, and even on short to intermediate routes, he can turn a three-yard catch or a 10-yard snag into something more. St. Brown will probably receive the most attention, which gives Williams a chance to break out and take advantage of the lackluster secondary. Williams has only gotten this line in three games this season, and he could've had it last week if he didn't drop a catch. Where Goff can find Williams is in play-action. Goff can have the offense believe it's a run and suddenly, Williams is downfield wide open. When it comes to play action, New England is in for a world of trouble. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.33 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown (-130) As I mentioned earlier, St. Brown has German ties and will want to show out for the "home" crowd. When reporters asked him Friday if he already had a touchdown celebration in mind because of the circumstances, he said: "I don't have it planned yet, I still have two days to figure that out. You know, I haven't been in the endzone in some weeks so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again." St. Brown is in a bit of a rut when it comes to finding the end zone, as he hasn't scored since Week 3. Five straight games without a touchdown is the longest he's gone without one since the end of the 2022 season, when he didn't score in the last five games. He also had seven straight games without a touchdown that season. This bet is strictly vibes-based and can sometimes be a bust, but I think the stars are aligning too much for you not to think the Lions and Goff won't have plays drawn up for him to score. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $17.69 If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +286 and $10 -> $38.66 Record: 11-13 Brandon's Bold Bet If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay: Jahmyr Gibbs 4+ receptions (-210) St. Brown over 7.5 receptions (+102) Jared Goff 3+ touchdowns (+225) For this week's bold bets, I am including running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but not for his ground game. The Patriots are averaging at least three passes per game to their running backs, and with the running game possibly limited, Detroit could use Gibbs more as a receiver this week to find success. Gibbs is averaging four catches a game, and he was held to none against Miami and only two against the Minnesota Vikings. I think he gets back on track this week with at least four. Speaking of the receiving game, St. Brown won't just find the end zone on Sunday; I think he will be a go-to option for Goff, which won't be surprising. St. Brown is averaging 7.6 catches a game this season, so I think he can hit eight. St. Brown will want to put on as much of a show as he can in Germany, so he seems like the best guy to lean on this week. Finally, my boldest pick this week is Goff to throw for at least three passing touchdowns. Goff has done this in only two games this season, but I think it'll be a high-scoring affair in Munich. Detroit may have to lean on the passing game and Goff, giving him a chance to score multiple times. New England is averaging 1.5 passing touchdowns a game and just allowed three passing touchdowns to Green Bay. Goff has a chance to rebound after last week's dud and show the world he's an MVP candidate. The worst fears of the New England Patriots might have been realized after quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury while playing the Detroit Lions on Sunday, November 15. Maye, 24, will miss "an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season," ESPN reported on Monday, November 16. The quarterback left the game, which took place in Munich, Germany, during the first quarter after he was sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson . Hutchinson, 26, also suffered a knee injury on the play after celebrating the sack. There is fear Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the season. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained that Maye did not immediately head home with the team. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly." Immediately after the game, Vrabel told reporters that Maye would "get more tests run" when he returned stateside. "He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level," Vrabel explained. Vrabel downplayed any malicious intent on Hutchinson's behalf, telling reporters, "I don't think it was anything intentional." Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito stepped in and played the rest of the game for the Patriots. The Lions dominated New England in Maye's absence, winning 35-10. "I'm going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point," DeVito said after Sunday's game. "Something that as a [backup], as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter. So just keep doing what I'm doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next."

Maye injured his ankle on a sack by Aidan Hutchinson in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss and didn't return. Vrabel said after the game that Maye would get tests done once home to determine the severity of the injury. During his news conference on Monday, Vrabel wouldn't confirm or deny that Maye will be out for an extended period. But he did say he would miss more time. 'I wouldnt imagine him being available when we come out of the bye,' Vrabel said. Top NFL insider Ian Rapoport has been blasted by a former New England Patriots reporter over a 'botched' update on star quarterback Drake Maye. The Patriots star suffered a right ankle injury during Sunday's brutal loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich and is feared to require season-ending surgery. However, Rapoport, who now works for ESPN following the network's acquisition of NFL Network earlier this year, posted on Sunday that Maye had already returned to New England. 'Maye came back from Germany and will seek more medical information,' Rapoport posted. That irked Alex Sims, who used to cover the Patriots for NESN, and she slammed the NFL insider on her own account. 'Another BOTCHED report,' she posted. 'As a former journalist, correct info over fast info is so much more important. Ok, I'm done.' Losers of two straight games and three of their last four, New England has a bye this week and won't play again until November 29 against the Los Angeles Chargers. 'He'll be traveling back here shortly, but (the team) just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely,' Vrabel added during his regularly scheduled radio interview with Bostons WEEI on the 'Greg Hill Show.' The coach said Sunday that he didn't consider the sack that injured Maye to be improper – Hutchinson had caught up to Maye and pulled him down from behind. 'I'm not going to assume there was something there,' Vrabel said. 'However it happened, I don't think it was anything intentional. I'm sure that it wasn't. That's part of the game.' Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison for New England after replacing Maye. The Patriots managed just 151 total yards on the day, a season low. The only other quarterback on the roster is Behren Morton, who is on the practice squad.

home.headline: Aidan Hutchinson injury update has Lions DE with torn ACL: Live updates
home.blurb: He is going to be out for the rest of the 2026 season with an ACL tear in his right knee , according to reports from two top NFL newsbreakers Monday morning. A few hours after the Lions won 35-10 for their fifth straight victory, reports came out that the team was "bracing for bad news" with the likelihood Hutchinson misses the rest of the season for the second time in three years. Hutchinson broke bones in his left leg in 2024 against Dallas on a sack. He made the Pro Bowl last season in his return to the field, recording a career-high 14½ sacks while playing all 17 games, and signed a mammoth new contract extension in October 2025 that begins in 2027. Aidan Hutchinson ACL tear has him out for season: Reports The Ringer's Tom Pelissero on Sunday afternoon was first to definitively report Hutchinson would be out for the season, but the injury was unclear. Now, we await an official announcement from the Lions, who arrived back in Michigan overnight. They are off Monday, ahead of this Sunday's home game against Tampa Bay (3-6) . Report: Aidan Hutchinson out for season He eventually walked off with medical personnel, underwent a lengthy evaluation in the blue medical tent on the Lions sideline and then walked to the locker room. He was ruled questionable initially and then ruled out in the third quarter. He reportedly then underwent an MRI and German media outlet Joyn posted a picture of Hutchinson on crutches outside of the Lions’ team bus. Aidan Hutchinson will be 'out for the season' Reporters started putting out information just before 2 p.m. ET that the Lions fear Hutchinson will be out for the season after a significant knee injury. The Ringer's Tom Pelissero had the strongest wording, saying, "Imaging in Munich confirmed the injury to Hutchinson, whose right knee buckled as he celebrated a sack against the Patriots. He’s out for the season." The Lions recorded four sacks of Patriots backup QB Tommy DeVito after Hutchinson's injury. (Drake Maye hurt his ankle on Hutchinson's sack and also did not return.) Hutchinson hurt his knee Sunday celebrating a first-quarter sack against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Hutchinson is the second Lions defensive captain to experience a significant injury in the past two weeks, after middle linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a spinal injury Nov. 1 and remains in a Detroit area hospital. home.headline: How is Jack Campbell doing? Latest injury update for Lions LB
home.blurb: A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football. Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season. It will mark the Lions second week without Jack Campbell after the linebacker suffered a neck injury during the Detroit's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . The 26-year-old laid motionless on the field and was eventually carted off as emotional teammates looked on . The Lions placed Campbell on injured reserve on Nov. 7, marking the last update provided on the player's condition. Updates have been few and far between, with the most notable news coming via a statement from Campbell on Nov. 4. In that update, the linebacker revealed he had movement in his lower body and was making progress with movement in his upper body. Detroit was victorious in its first game without Campbell, winning 19-9 over the Miami Dolphins in Week 9 . The Lions face a step up in competition as the schedule shifts to Week 10, where the New England Patriots await in Germany. picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Falcons vs. Chiefs Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back on track in Week 10, but they face a difficult challenge with Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster. Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies. How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions. Scott Kennedy (4-5) The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year. Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline. Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense. We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face. Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17 Gerald Thomas, III (4-5) The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away. Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought. The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense . Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft. Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21 Garrett Chapman (4-5) The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates. On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him. This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now. Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17 Darius Hayes (4-5) Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference. Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack. The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense. Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory. Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast , (4-5) Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team. There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run. The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates). On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls. This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story. Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16 Final Predictions: Chiefs Are the Unanimous Pick Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10. The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday. For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense. Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and will be shown on CBS. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Falcons: NFL Week 10 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI As the 2026-27 season rolls through to Week 10, the trade deadline and over half a campaign of play are in the books. It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall. Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group? With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win. Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs. The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta. It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless. Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr. Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts. I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish. Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened. Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team. This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them. On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson. I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. They are getting further and further away from their wins over the 6-3 Packers and 7-1 49ers, however. Published Nov 15, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Chiefs are 3.5-point favorites over the Falcons on the spread, with the over/under set at 47.5 total points. Kansas City is a -172 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Atlanta is a +144 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Chiefs vs Falcons predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 15. Chiefs vs Falcons Prediction Chiefs vs Falcons pick: Falcons +3.5 (-120) My Falcons vs. Chiefs best bet is Atlanta to cover the spread. Chiefs vs Falcons NFL Week 10 Odds Chiefs vs Falcons spread : Chiefs -3.5 (+100), Falcons +3.5 (-120) Chiefs vs Falcons total : over/under 47.5 (-110o / -110u) Chiefs vs Falcons moneyline : Chiefs -172, Falcons +144 Chiefs vs Falcons NFL Week 10 Betting Preview Kansas City Chiefs Preview: Don't Be Fooled By KC's Strong Record The Chiefs are rolling into Atlanta in a very questionable spot as this marks their third road game in four weeks. Despite the brand name and the record, this is simply not the same Chiefs offense of old. Patrick Mahomes suffered an injury to his throwing elbow last week against the Jets and likely won't be 100% for this game even if he suits up. Over the last four games, his average depth of target (aDOT) and air yards have plummeted, sitting at 3.6, 4.7, 4.7, and 3.6. The Chiefs' downfield passing attack is virtually non-existent at this point. They are leaning heavily on the short, dink-and-dunk passing game, and that will probably continue following the addition of Josh Downs . Mahomes is having his worst year by far when facing defensive pressure. If you can collapse the pocket on him, the explosive plays vanish and the offense gets bogged down. Atlanta Falcons Preview: The Buy-Low Opportunity We might have officially reached the bottom of the market for the Falcons . And When you pair an elite pass rush against this version of Patrick Mahomes who is statistically having the worst season of his career under pressure, you have a recipe for defensive stops. The Chiefs will try to run the ball down Atlanta's throat with Kenneth Walker III , but Atlanta's defense is better than what it has showed in recent weeks. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They've got the league's best RB and a streaky young QB– it's an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they're more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. I'm excited to see what the Chiefs' offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I'm keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team's snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won't be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn't traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn't need a pass to win. This game should be a comfortable win for Kansas City because of its offense, leaning on the ground game once again to stay in rhtyhm and open up the middle of the field for passes. 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson All nine panelists predicted the Chiefs to win by more than ten points. Only 50.6% of our readers anticipated a comfortable Chiefs victory, while 37.2% expected Mahomes and Company to narrowly come out on top. 12.2% of respondents expected the Jets to win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

(Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty Nick Roesch · HEAVY Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:51 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs wrapped their final practice of the week on Friday ahead on their road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Kansas City is dealing with a few key injuries that could impact Sunday's game. The headliner is running back Kenneth Walker III, who is questionable to play after sustaining a groin injury. Of course, when injuries occur, it provides an opportunity for someone else to step up. Joshua Ezeudu Will Start in Place of Jaylon Moore for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Falcons Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained an ankle injury during last week's win over the New York Jets . He has been ruled out against Atlanta after not participating in any practices this week. Getting the start in his place will be Joshua Ezeudu, who the Chiefs acquired in a trade with the New York Giants back in August. Ezeudu was a third-round draft pick by the Giants in 2022. He appeared in 16 games for New York during his four-year tenure, starting 10. A calf injury cost him the entire 2025 season. Ezeudu started for Moore in Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks . While speaking to the media on Friday, coach Andy Reid gave Ezeudu a big vote of confidence. "We feel comfortable with him in there," Reid said. "He did a nice job for us last week, and the other times that he's had to fill in." Chiefs' Final Week 10 Injury Report Here is the final injury report for Kansas City's matchup against the Falcons: RT Jaylon Moore- Out (Ankle) DT Peter Woods- Out (Neck) DT Omarr Norman-Lott- Out (Knee) RB Kenneth Walker III- Questionable (Groin) RB Jayden Ott- Questionable (Hamstring) CB Mansoor Delane- Questionable (Shoulder) WR Xavier Worthy- No Designation (Hamstring) QB Justin Fields- No Designation (Neck) LB Jeffrey Bassa- No Designation (Hand) S Jaden Hicks- No Designation (Shoulder) TE Travis Kelce- No Designation (Ankle) QB Patrick Mahomes- No Designation (Knee, Elbow) WR Rashee Rice- No Designation (Knee) Like Moore, Woods also missed the entire week of practice. He injured his neck back in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos , which Reid has called a "stinger." Delane has also missed the last two games with a shoulder injury that has plagued him since OTAs. Worthy made rapid progress after hurting his hamstring against the Jets last week and is good to go against Atlanta. The same can be said for Mahomes' elbow injury, which gave the Chiefs a scare last week. Norman-Lott continues to ramp up toward making his season debut, possibly as soon as next week. away.headline: Chiefs battled through more injury problems in victory over Atlanta Falcons
away.blurb: “I thought guys that stepped in really helped us out,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Johnson demonstrated his readiness for more work based on his performance in Denver two weeks ago, when he accounted for 143 combined yards plus a 44-yard kickoff return. Walker’s status for the next game, Sunday at home against the Arizona Cardinals, won’t be known until later this week. Reid announced the injury on Friday and didn’t rule Walker out until the next day. Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 despite injuries across the offense. Emmett Johnson posted 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two scores. Jared Wiley fractured an ankle, and Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs went to Atlanta for Sunday’s showdown against the Falcons without their leading rusher and starting right tackle. During the game, they lost their right guard and backup tight end. Meanwhile, star tight end Travis Kelce hobbled off the field and center starting Creed Humphrey left the game after getting his eye poked. The Chiefs survived it all, even thrived, in defeating the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 partly because the replacements didn’t miss a beat. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made the biggest splash. He got his first NFL start in place of Kenneth Walker, who showed up on the injury report late in the week with a strained groin. Against the Falcons he was even better, leading the Chiefs in both rushing — 101 yards — and receiving. He had six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Chiefs tight end Jared Wiley suffered the most serious injury, fracturing an ankle. That happened in the first quarter. Kelce’s injury occurred when he was tackled after a 23-yard reception. Reid said Kelce, who has been dealing with ankle problems this year, injured his calf. He re-entered the game in the second quarter. “He got twisted up a little bit,” Reid said. The tight end position continued to produce in spite of the injuries, with Jake Briningstool hauling in a 20-yard catch, the longest of his nine-game NFL career. Also in the first quarter, guard Trey Smith left the game and Reid said he has entered the concussion protocol. Mike Caliendo, who had played left guard instead of Kingsley Suamataia in two games this season, filled in for Smith. Elsewhere on the offensive line, center Creed Humphrey took a finger in the face and left the game. Television replays showed a cut under his eye. Mike Nourzad got some snaps before Humphrey returned. Besides Walker, the Chiefs entered the game without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed the start with an ankle injury. Josh Ezeudu made his second start of the season. It appeared rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who has missed time with a shoulder injury, may have re-injured himself. But Reid said he should be OK. “He landed on his back, near that shoulder area,” Reid said. “I think he scared him more than anything. He’s going to be all right.” This story was originally published November 15, 2026 at 5:19 PM . Chiefs’ report card reflects

away.blurb: Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker. From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
away.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. home.headline: Chiefs battled through more injury problems in victory over Atlanta Falcons
home.blurb: “I thought guys that stepped in really helped us out,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Johnson demonstrated his readiness for more work based on his performance in Denver two weeks ago, when he accounted for 143 combined yards plus a 44-yard kickoff return. Walker’s status for the next game, Sunday at home against the Arizona Cardinals, won’t be known until later this week. Reid announced the injury on Friday and didn’t rule Walker out until the next day. Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 despite injuries across the offense. Emmett Johnson posted 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two scores. Jared Wiley fractured an ankle, and Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs went to Atlanta for Sunday’s showdown against the Falcons without their leading rusher and starting right tackle. During the game, they lost their right guard and backup tight end. Meanwhile, star tight end Travis Kelce hobbled off the field and center starting Creed Humphrey left the game after getting his eye poked. The Chiefs survived it all, even thrived, in defeating the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 partly because the replacements didn’t miss a beat. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made the biggest splash. He got his first NFL start in place of Kenneth Walker, who showed up on the injury report late in the week with a strained groin. Against the Falcons he was even better, leading the Chiefs in both rushing — 101 yards — and receiving. He had six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Chiefs tight end Jared Wiley suffered the most serious injury, fracturing an ankle. That happened in the first quarter. Kelce’s injury occurred when he was tackled after a 23-yard reception. Reid said Kelce, who has been dealing with ankle problems this year, injured his calf. He re-entered the game in the second quarter. “He got twisted up a little bit,” Reid said. The tight end position continued to produce in spite of the injuries, with Jake Briningstool hauling in a 20-yard catch, the longest of his nine-game NFL career. Also in the first quarter, guard Trey Smith left the game and Reid said he has entered the concussion protocol. Mike Caliendo, who had played left guard instead of Kingsley Suamataia in two games this season, filled in for Smith. Elsewhere on the offensive line, center Creed Humphrey took a finger in the face and left the game. Television replays showed a cut under his eye. Mike Nourzad got some snaps before Humphrey returned. Besides Walker, the Chiefs entered the game without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed the start with an ankle injury. Josh Ezeudu made his second start of the season. It appeared rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who has missed time with a shoulder injury, may have re-injured himself. But Reid said he should be OK. “He landed on his back, near that shoulder area,” Reid said. “I think he scared him more than anything. He’s going to be all right.” This story was originally published November 15, 2026 at 5:19 PM . Chiefs’ report card reflects

home.headline: Kenneth Walker Injured, Latest Rumors on Chiefs RB vs. Falcons and Emmett Johnson Fantasy Outlook
home.blurb: Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker. From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

picks.blurb: Texans vs. Browns: Final Score Predictions by Experts for Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Texans vs. Browns: Final Score Predictions by Experts for Week 10 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Houston Texans enter Sunday's road game against the Cleveland Browns as 4.5-point favorites. The Browns have a better 5-4 record and a strong home defense, but their offensive struggles and Deshaun Watson's vulnerability under pressure have influenced many experts to favor Houston. The Texans have attracted support because of their explosive passing game and league-leading pass rush. But not every expert expects Houston to cover the spread. Some believe the Browns can use their home advantage and defensive pressure to keep Stroud from taking control. The predictions therefore point toward Houston as the more popular winner, but not necessarily an easy afternoon for the visitors. Picks: Texans 3 Browns 0 "Deshaun Watson should be back in the lineup, but the receiver matchup against Houston is favorable, with the Texans allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to WRs. Both rookies are worth considering as flex options," Eric Moody says. Houston has a 76.1% chance to win as per ESPN , while Daniel Oyefusi believes the Browns defense will have a bad time against C.J. Stroud and company. "The Texans are 9-3 ATS against the Browns since 2005. Cleveland's protection problems give Houston another opening. The Browns allow sacks at the league's highest rate, while Houston has the second-highest sack rate," Pamela Maldonado wrote. Picks: Texans 5, Browns 0 Brooke Cersosimo points out the Texans averaging 8.2 yards per passing play in 257 snaps Nico Collins has played. This is more than the San Francisco 49ers' league-leading 7.9. "Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy….Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team," Cersosimo says. Bleacher Report Picks: Texans 6, Browns 1 Only Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford believes Cleveland can actually get past the Texans on Sunday. "The Texans probably see this as a revenge game as much as Watson does, but I think the Browns are able to muddy this one up for C.J. Stroud just enough to stay in the game, like we've seen them do multiple times this season," Hanford says of the Browns. Meanwhile, Brent Sobleski has a contrasting view. "It doesn't matter which quarterback is starting for the Browns, because the Texans defense should make their life miserable, even if that unit has been somewhat of a disappointment this season," Sobleski writes. Dawgs By Nature Picks: Texans 3, Browns 3 The balanced picks come as analyst Chris Pokorny believes C.J. Stroud's elite passing form collides directly with Cleveland's biggest strength, a disciplined, reliable pass defense. Dawgs By Nature's Thomas Moore picked the Browns but is still frustrated with Cleveland's erratic form since they lost winnable games against the New York Jets and New Orleans Saints. Moore knows how good the 3-5 Texans are but 2 of their 3 victories came against the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. Barry Shuck, who picked Houston, says, "Before the season began, I believed that the Texans would be one of the four best teams in the AFC. The Texans have a prolific passing attack and the Browns are ranked #13 against the pass, so that will be a good chess match. They can't run the ball, but neither can the Browns. Cleveland is middle of the pack in their passing game while Houston is listed in the lower third defending the pass. So, maybe the Browns can air it out to Harold Fannin and either of their two rookie receivers." The Arizona Republic "The Browns are 3-0 at home this season, but in the midst of a two-game losing skid. Cleveland won't be able to keep up with C.J. Stroud and the Texans, even if this game is at home," Jeremy Cluff says. Cluff's predicted scoreline: Texans 23, Browns 14 What Do These Predictions Mean? Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud gestures during the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium.Kirby Lee - Imagn Images Houston enters as a 4.5-point favorite (-4.5), while Cleveland is a 4.5-point underdog (+4.5). This means Houston must win by at least five points to cover the spread. Historically, the Texans and Browns are tied at 7-7 in their regular-season series. However, Houston secured a 45-14 victory over Cleveland in their Wild Card round matchup on January 13, 2024. Houston will be looking to continue its success against Cleveland in Week 10. picks.blurb: Week 10 picks: Who the experts are taking in Texans vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Week 10 picks: Who the experts are taking in Texans vs. Browns Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads So, is this the week when the Houston Texans begin a new winning streak? Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. They use their hands and they play really hard continuously. They're a handful for sure." As for Houston, quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. How do the experts feel about Sunday's showdown between a pair of AFC dark horses desperate to pick up a win for different reasons? Here are their thoughts entering the battle in Huntington Bank Stadium. Texans could be missing exactly what they needed to exploit the Browns' biggest weakness The Texans were shaping up to be an extremely tough matchup for Cleveland, and they probably still are. No quarterback, meanwhile, has been sacked more than Deshaun Watson, who’s been taken down 33 times in eight games. Keeping Watson upright will be one of the keys to this game regardless of who’s rushing off the edges.
