picks.blurb: Updated: Predicting Packers-Vikings Winner, Plus Final Record, Playoffs and More Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers will renew their border war against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Initially, I had the Vikings beat the Packers 20-17. I’m perhaps guilty of overvaluing Cousins based on his stats this season and his play against Green Bay over the years, but I think he’s good enough to make the Vikings a legit contender. He’s not good enough to carry an offense, though. On Friday, the Vikings ruled out tight end T.J. Hockenson and receiver Jauan Jennings. Helped by Cousins, Hockenson caught 86 passes in 2022 and 95 passes in 2023. On Sunday, the Vikings listed receiver Jordan Addison among their inactives due to a finger injury. At full strength, few quarterbacks could match Justin Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson for a Big Three. On Sunday, Cousins will be throwing to Jefferson, receiver Tai Felton (three catches) and tight end Gavin Bartholomew (seven catches). So, let’s flip-flop the original prediction. Packers 20, Vikings 17. Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. My Vikings vs. Packers prediction and NFL picks say Kirk Cousins' emergency return to Minnesota won't be enough to survive an NFC North clash at Lambeau Field, where Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams are primed to power a Green Bay victory. "Cap'n Kirk is coming back!" was the immediate text sent to family when news broke that veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins was traded back to the Minnesota Vikings earlier this week. It was an emergency move to rescue a floundering offense wasting Brian Flores' dominant defense. Here are my expert NFL best bets ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. TOP PICK Vikings vs Packers prediction today: Packers moneyline The move to bring back Kirk Cousins is an upgrade for the Minnesota Vikings offense, but a half-cooked Cousins isn't going to be enough at Lambeau Field. Not with the tread wearing thin on this Minnesota defense. The Vikings' stop unit is playing on a short week after logging more than 42 minutes of work in Monday's loss to the Bills. Minnesota has spent an average of 36:41 on the field over the last three weeks , and the wear and tear is starting to show. Linebackers Blake Cashman (concussion) and Kyle Van Noy (calf) run the risk of missing Week 10. The Green Bay Packers are a long way removed from the team that lost to the Vikings in Week 1. Green Bay has been one of the best two-way teams since Week 6, ranking Top 10 in both EPA per play and EPA allowed in that span. There are some injury concerns for the Cheeseheads, which is why I'm going with the outright price and not laying -3.5. Vikings vs Packers combo The Cousins deal doesn't do much for me, and only offers better return on the Packers' moneyline at home. This Vikings stop unit is great, but it's possibly down some key guys and playing on a short week after logging major minutes on MNF. Tucker Kraft had a nice day against the Vikings in Week 1 and has been a red zone threat in recent weeks, with two TDs in his last three games. Savion Williams could be just what the Packers need to bust this Vikings defense. The burly slot receiver is a quick hitter who can pick up yards after the catch. His projections sit as high as 24+ yards in Week 10. Packers moneyline Tucker Kraft anytime touchdown Savion Williams 20+ receiving yards Vikings vs Packers touchdown scorer: Tucker Kraft The Packers have been able to strike for some home run touchdowns in recent weeks, but things shorten up against this Vikings defense. The Cheeseheads will have to work for six points when they enter the red zone. Kraft is a popular target, drawing nine passes inside the 20-yard line for seven receptions and three touchdowns. Kraft does his best work against zone coverage — which is something Brian Flores utilizes almost exclusively — and may catch a break if Cashman sits, as he's Minnesota's top coverage linebacker. Williams has stepped into the WR3 role, giving Love a big target in the slot. He's caught 11 of 13 targets for game outputs of five, 25, 32, and 47 yards. Both head coach Matt LaFleur and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich gushed about Williams' skill set heading into Week 10, seeing the 6-foot-4, 222-pound receiver as a bigger part of the plan. "We're going to continue to try to find ways to get him the ball," LaFleur told the media. "You just see the power that he has." Given this Vikings defense's aggressive approach, Williams' role as a slot receiver becomes even more vital, with Love looking for a quick release from pressure. The Vikings have been exposed by slot options, most recently allowing the Bills' Khalil Shakir to pick up 58 yards on four receptions. The Packers are 2.5-point favorites on the spread (Packers -2.5; -120), with the over/under set at 42.5 (-105o / -115u). Green Bay is a -146 moneyline favorite while Minnesota is a +124 underdog. Vikings vs Packers Odds Vikings vs Packers Spread : Vikings +2.5 (+100), Packers -2.5 (-120) Vikings vs Packers Over/Under : 42.5 (-105o / -115u) Vikings vs Packers Moneyline : Vikings +124, Packers -146 Vikings vs Packers Preview Vikings Preview The Vikings are stepping into a difficult situational spot for this showdown game against the Packers on a short week of rest. After an exhausting Monday night loss to Buffalo in which the Vikings defense was forced to be on the field for 42 minutes and over 75 plays, the gas tank is going to be completely empty. Because of that workload, the injuries are starting to pile up. Star linebacker Blake Cashman suffered a concussion and will likely miss this game, and T.J. Hockenson is also banged up. Of course, the big news on the offensive side of the ball is Kirk Cousins coming over via trade from the Raiders to provide competence at the quarterback position that's been lacking all season. While Cousins is an upgrade over Carson Wentz/ Kyler Murray and should help stabilize the play-action game, the timing and rhythm of a brand-new quarterback operating on a short week are concerning. Packers Preview The Green Bay Packers are quietly rounding into elite form on the defensive side of the ball. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon is doing a tremendous schematic job, changing up coverages, getting consistent pressure, and throwing complex looks to confuse quarterbacks. Despite dealing with injuries, the Packers have operated at a top-five level over the past month. Offensively, head coach Matt LaFleur deserves a ton of credit. The Packers essentially have no offensive line, and the run game is non-existent with Josh Jacobs out, yet they continue to successfully push the ball downfield with Jordan Love consistently hitting home runs to Matthew Golden and Christian Watson . The vertical passing attack is precisely how you have to attack the Vikings' aggressive defense, which sets up well for Green Bay here. The Packers lost the first meeting with the Vikings earlier this season but performed well, outgaining Minnesota by nearly 200 yards before things got weird late. The Packers will have the advantage of already having tape and familiarity against Flores' blitz packages. After getting embarrassed in Week 1 by the Vikings, this is a revenge game for a Packers team that is 5-1 in their last six games. Minnesota recently traded for Kirk Cousins, so that's been one of the key talking points going into this one. Green Bay is a bit banged up , but so is every team at this point in the season. For the second time this year, the Vikings are able to avoid Micah Parsons, though Minnesota is out a pair of key players themselves. Cousins has thrown an interception in five of the nine games he's played this year. His season began with a two-interception game against the Miami Dolphins, and he's fresh off a three-interception contest in San Francisco. This Packers defense has been on an absolute tear, and even with Xavier McKinney being questionable, there are more than enough playmakers who can capitalize on the 38-year-old's return to the Vikings. There could be a few reasons for why this happens, but Green Bay needs a big game from Kaleb Johnson. Johnson looked great in Week 9 when Josh Jacobs broke his finger, and if there was ever a time to get the run game going, it's against this Vikings defense. Sure, Love is coming off a monstrous 372-yard performance, but Minnesota isn't about to let him throw for nearly 400 yards again. Love has thrown for 300+ yards four times this season. He's finished with at least 274 passing yards in each of his last five games. Obviously, Packers fans will try to go against this prediction as he threw for 387 yards in Week 1, but Minnesota's defense has only gotten better since that point. Lambeau Field is going to be in for a treat on Sunday, Nov. 15. The NFC North has proven it's the best division in all of football, and Matt LaFleur's squad is going to go all out with a bye next weekend. Trey Smack has had his fair share of struggles this season, but he's also been locked in throughout a few key moments. In all likelihood, this will be a close game that comes down to the wire, so every point matters, and there's a real chance the Packers could give Smack a chance to win the game.

He just needs to do what he's done this season for the Raiders and throughout his career, which is to distribute the football and bring a high floor to the passing game. If he can do that, the Vikings should be in every game because of their elite defense. The first test comes on Sunday afternoon at Lambeau Field, against MVP candidate Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. It's a massive game in the NFL's most competitive division, with the Vikings having an opportunity to complete a sweep over the Packers and secure a head-to-head tiebreaker. Here are our staff writers' score predictions. Read BMTN without the ads. BMTN Premium: The latest BMTN and BMTS stories ad-free, plus Weather+ with Sven Sundgaard. $6.99/month or $60/annual → Will Ragatz: Packers 24, Vikings 20 The Vikings absolutely can win this game, with Cousins providing a boost to the offense and Brian Flores' defense doing its thing. But it's hard to sweep a division rival, especially one as good as the Packers. Jordan Love is playing at an extremely high level right now and should have some answers to Minnesota's blitzes. I don't love that the Vikings are without Blake Cashman, who is the MVP of their defense and one of the best linebackers in football. Cousins could also have a little rust in his first week with his new/old team. For those reasons, it feels safer to pick Green Bay. Joe Nelson: Vikings 27, Packers 23 Jordan Love scares me. He's playing at an MVP level and making deep throws look as simple as a checkdown. It's truly terrifying. But Minnesota destroyed him in the second half of the season opener, and without Josh Jacobs, the Packers should be one-dimensional. That gives the NFL's best defense the edge, even if middle linebacker Blake Cashman misses the game. Meanwhile, the Vikings' offense is going to finally look functional with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Justin Jefferson will get back to his annual routine of torching the Packers, and the Vikings will leave Lambeau Field with newfound Super Bowl hopes. Tony Liebert: Packers 31, Vikings 30 The Vikings ripped off the band-aid and made the right move to trade for Kirk Cousins, but immediately going into Lambeau Field is a tough task for any quarterback. The Packers' offense has begun to find something through the air with Matthew Golden emerging as a breakout star. I think Brian Flores will have a gameplan to get Green Bay out of its flow offensively, but the Vikings' offense also has a slow start with Cousins. The Packers will make one more play than Minnesota in a close one. Jonathan Harrison: Vikings 21, Packers 15 Jordan Love is playing at an unreal level lately. So has the Vikings' defense this season. Which wins out? That will come down to how well the Vikings' offense operates. With Kirk back, the offense is expected to just be fixed. However, he's practiced twice this week. That's not a lot of time to get settled back in. If he's able to just keep the offense on the field and sustain drives, then the Vikings' defense will be able to stay healthy and make Love's day miserable. I think that is the likeliest scenario. It won't be pretty, but it will be encouraging going forward as Kirk gets reacquainted with KOC's offense. Adam Uren: Packers 24, Vikings 13 Kirk Cousins is the new Vikings quarterback so everything's good, right? Wrong. The Vikings may have taken steps to fix their abysmal offense, but Rome wasn't rebuilt in a day, or something. I have an inkling that, under the hood, the dysfunction runs deeper than just the signal caller, so I expect the defense will once again be on the field long enough for them to tire, and for Jordan Love to find Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in space one too many times. While none of the four analysts gave score predictions, they all predict the Minnesota Vikings will improve to 7-2 with a statement win at Lambeau Field. Louis Riddick, Andrew Hawkins, Will Compton, and Taylor Lewan all chose the Vikings over the Packers in Sunday's NFC North showdown. It's important to remember what the Vikings did to GB in Week 1, though that game was played in Minnesota. Packers fans will go back to the officials in that one, but ultimately, there's no excuse for giving up 29 unanswered points. It feels like those days are behind the Packers, but with head coach Matt LaFleur at the helm, anything can happen on Sunday, Nov. 15. Micah Parsons is still two weeks out from returning, but this Packers defense has been unbelievable the past few weeks. There were a few breakdowns in coverage against the New England Patriots, but it didn't matter as Jordan Love played out of his mind . Love leads the league in passing, and one could argue he now has the most dynamic receiving duo in the NFL. On the other side, Justin Jefferson is stuck doing absolutely nothing in this Vikings offense. He has just 31 receptions for 393 yards this season. For reference, Love threw for 387 yards in Week 1. Tucker Kraft, who's coming off a torn ACL, is only 42 yards shy of Jefferson's total this season. Both Matthew Golden (14.8) and Christian Watson (17.9) are well ahead of Jefferson's 12.7 yards per reception, and it's really not even close. Now with Kirk Cousins back, it should give Jefferson an opportunity to emerge as a dominant WR1 once again. Once Carson Wentz came into the game in Week 1, Jefferson exploded with his best game of the year. He finished with eight receptions on nine targets for 92 yards with a pair of touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has had plenty of time to settle into his new role, so now just over two months later, it'll be interesting to see what adjustments he makes. No one is denying the fact that the Vikings' defense is legit, but Love has blossomed into a true MVP candidate this season, and with what he did against Minnesota in Week 1, it's crazy to think the entire Get Up crew predicted the Packers would fall to 6-4.

away.headline: Kyler Murray Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Vikings QB's Return Timeline After Kirk Cousins Trade
away.blurb: The 29-year-old quarterback could be targeting Minnesota's Week 12 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons for his potential return, according to Pelissero. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. Murray's absence doesn't seem as urgent after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round draft pick. If Cousins misses time, the team will have to turn to Carson Wentz, who is serving as the backup in Murray's absence. Cousins to Make NFL History Today Murray suffered the injury during a 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. He also missed Week 2 after suffering a concussion in Minnesota's regular-season opener. Although Murray compiled a 5-1 record as a starter this season, he was at the helm of a struggling Vikings offense. The eighth-year quarterback has just 1,022 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. Wentz struggled mightily when he stepped in for Murray on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 32 percent of his passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota showed interest in reuniting with Cousins prior to Monday night , but Wentz' poor performance likely made it easier for the Vikings to name Cousins as the starter for a pivotal matchup against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10. Cousins is already familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive system from the last two seasons of his six-year stint in Minnesota. He also has plenty of chemistry with star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who enjoyed his most productive years on the receiving end of Cousins' passes. Cousins and O'Connell both struggled after parting ways, but they now have an opportunity to make up for lost time. Still, Murray's availability could prove valuable behind a 38-year-old quarterback. away.headline: Vikings-Packers Second Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. home.headline: Packers edge defender is quietly rewriting his career story, and Micah Parsons' return could make him even more dangerous
home.blurb: Packers edge defender is quietly rewriting his career story, and Micah Parsons' return could make him even more dangerous - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Parsons' return changes the math Micah Parsons is now slated to return potentially as soon as Week 12 against the Los Angeles Rams. That should give Van Ness an even bigger role than the one he has now. Opposing offenses will shift their attention toward Parsons once he is back on the field. As a result, Van Ness should see more one-on-one matchups and more pass-rushing opportunities against favorable looks. A player who already leads the team in pressures without that help could become far more productive with it. Van Ness has been EDGE1 for the Packers this season, and he will become EDGE2 when Parsons returns. That is a demotion on paper only. In practice, it is the best possible setup for his game, and he will still play a lot of snaps. Van Ness arrived as a first-round pick in 2023 with the selection Green Bay acquired from the New York Jets in the Aaron Rodgers trade. At the time, the team did not expect him to start, and he didn't become a starter until this season. Even last year his playing time was limited behind Micah Parsons and Rashan Gary. Van Ness was essentially the third rotational piece. He also suffered a foot injury that affected his entire season. He is finally healthy and has little competition for snaps, and the results show it. The fifth-year option keeps Van Ness under contract with the Packers through 2027, with $13.75 million fully guaranteed for next year. The upcoming offseason could be a natural point to discuss a contract extension. It's not clear whether Green Bay will go that route or let Van Ness play out his deal. Still, he has earned a raise, or at least some sort of adjustment to his contract. The financial angle also favors a deal. By signing Van Ness to an extension, the Packers could potentially lower his cap hit in 2027 and lock in a player who is entering his prime. For a front office that has long valued developing its own pass rushers, that would be a logical way to reward a draft pick who took longer than expected to break through. Van Ness may never fully settle the debate about his draft slot. His fourth season has changed the conversation, though, and Parsons' return could make his case even stronger. home.headline: Micah Parsons Injury, Timeline Updated by Packers' HC as Star Still Has 'Hurdles to Clear'
home.blurb: Micah Parsons is on track to return to the field for the Green Bay Packers before Thanksgiving. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team plans on having the star pass-rusher available for its Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, even though he still has a "couple more hurdles to clear," per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Parsons' return will give the Packers a much-needed boost, as he is one of the best defensive players in the league with a resume that includes three First-Team All-Pro selections, five Pro Bowl nods and five seasons with double-digit sacks. It seems like that return is on track for the next time the team takes the field. LaFleur also said Green Bay will "see where he is by the end of the week." Parsons hasn't played this season as he recovers from a torn ACL he suffered in December. He missed the rest of the 2025 campaign for Green Bay, including its postseason loss to the rival Chicago Bears. However, he might finally be on the field again for the NFC North club, which opened his practice window earlier this month. Green Bay is on a bye for Week 11, so he has a bit more time to get ready for a Wednesday game. This is also a critical time for the Packers in the postseason chase, as Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings dropped them to 6-4 and in last place in the competitive NFC North. Every other team in the division has just two losses, so the focus may eventually have to shift to the wild-card race. And that game against the Rams is a critical one. Green Bay, Los Angeles and the Seattle Seahawks are all 6-4 and tied in the race for the seventh and final seed in the NFC playoff picture. The Packers have the spot as of Monday because of conference record, but a head-to-head result against the Rams will go a long way toward determining wild-card positioning.

home.headline: Packers list 12 players with status designations on final Week 10 injury report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players with status designations on the final Week 10 injury report, including seven players listed as questionable to play on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings . Of the 12, three are designated to return from injury lists and are not part of the 53-man roster, so nine players -- or roughly 17 percent of the roster -- have status designations for Sunday. Edge rusher Micah Parsons, running back Josh Jacobs, center Sean Rhyan and tight end Josh Whyle were ruled out on Friday, while linebacker Zaire Franklin -- who has missed three straight games and didn't practice this week -- is doubtful to play. Parsons is still ramping up after returning to practice last week, Jacobs needs surgery on his broken finger, Rhyan will miss his third straight game with an ankle injury and Whyle is out for the second straight game due to a concussion. The seven players listed as questionable, with associated injuries: McKinney was a late add to the injury report on Friday with a foot injury. Brooks and Moore are designated to return from injured reserve but would need to be activated to the 53-man roster on Saturday to play Sunday. Van Ness and Bullard didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday with new injuries but returned in a limited capacity on Friday. Zeitler added a new injury (triceps) before Friday's practice and didn't participate. Inactives are released 90 minutes before kickoff, so we likely won't know more about the seven players listed as questionable to play until around 10:30 a.m. CT on Sunday morning. G Kevin Zeitler (ankle, triceps) Expect several roster moves on Saturday. The Packers need to activate Brooks and/or Moore to the 53 and elevate one or two players from the practice squad to the gameday roster for Week 10. But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week. “I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week. "It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice." How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans. Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late. The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate. But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. The Jaguars are rolling at 6-2 and have been dominating their opponents all season. Jacksonville has four wins by at least 23 points this year. No other team in the league has more than one such victory. The Titans, on the other hand, are in last place in the AFC South with a 1-7 record and have (again) started to rebuild for the future. Gone are star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who is one of the best defensive players in the entire league, and safety Amani Hooker, who leads the NFL with five interceptions. Both were traded before the NFL's trade deadline this past Tuesday. Trading Simmons netted the Titans two first-round picks from the Chicago Bears , while trading Hooker (and a fifth-rounder) to the Buffalo Bills brought back a second-round pick. On paper, this game looks like a mismatch. Jacksonville is one of the NFL's elite teams, while Tennessee is one of the worst. In addition to Simmons and Hooker, the Titans will also be without five injured starters on Sunday, including top rookies WR Carnell Tate and LB Anthony Hill Jr. However, it is still a divisional matchup, which is always tough no matter each team's record. Not taking Tennessee lightly was the first of my five keys to a Jaguars victory. If Jacksonville remains as focused on the Titans as it was on the Colts and Ravens in the past two weeks, this one could get ugly quickly. If the Jaguars get caught looking ahead to next week's road tilt against the first-place New York Giants , Jacksonville could fall victim to a huge upset. Don't bet on that happening. Jacksonville's high-powered offense will be going against a Tennessee defense that ranks 31st in both total yards and passing yards allowed. The Titans give up about 382 yards per game, 258 of which come through the air. Their run defense gives up about 124 yards per game, which is still only 22nd in the NFL. Tennessee gives up 24.9 points per game, which ranks 23rd. Those numbers were all with Simmons and Hooker. Jacksonville's offense, meanwhile, is averaging about 346 yards per game, and its average of 28.6 points per contest is the fourth-most in the league. Trevor Lawrence and Co. should have a field day. Defensively, the Jaguars give up only 15.1 points per game, the second-fewest in the league. Their run defense ranks fifth at about 89 yards per game. That is after the Jaguars gave up 172 rushing yards against Baltimore last week, many of which came during garbage time of Jacksonville's 33–10 win. The Jaguars should be able to dominate for the third week in a row. Unless Jacksonville gets caught looking past the Titans, the team should easily improve to 7-2 and continue flexing its muscles as one of the NFL's top Super Bowl contenders. Given the results of Jacksonville's last two games against inferior opponents, I don't expect the Jaguars to fall victim to a trap game. Prediction: Jaguars 38, Titans 9

Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Carnell Tate Out vs. Jaguars: Why it's Bad News for Cam Ward, But Will Help Titans' Draft Process Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. home.headline: Tennessee Titans place starter on injured reserve ahead of Week 11 vs. Dallas Cowboys
home.blurb: The Tennessee Titans have been trying to figure things out, but they are going to be without one of their key playmakers. ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson will be placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury suffered in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The earliest that Robinson can return would be Week 15 against the Indianapolis Colts. They also have rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate dealing with a shoulder injury, but it is not deemed to be as significant. It will be intriguing to see how significant the ankle injury is and what the Tennessee Titans look like over the remainder of the season. ・ Green Bay Packers Confirm Micah Parsons Return Plan Ahead of Week 11 The Tennessee Titans have been one of the young teams that have been struggling this season. They are in the mix for the top spot in the 2027 NFL Draft, but they can surprise a lot of people if they play well in the second half of the regular season. It is going to be a little more difficult following the recent news regarding one of their starters. Let’s take a closer look at who it is, what happened, and what it means for the Tennessee Titans going forward. Tennessee Titans place Wan’Dale Robinson on injured reserve Robinson has been struggling to get going this season as he has recorded 38 receptions on 54 targets for 272 yards (7.2 yards per catch) with three touchdowns. Robinson has recorded the most catches for the Tennessee Titans thus far, so this is going to be a major blow for quarterback Cam Ward’s progression as well. This decision also plays a major role for the New York Giants, who receive a compensatory pick from Robinson. He has been slightly above the fourth/fifth round bubble and being placed on injured reserve makes that a lot more difficult. As a result of the Tennessee Titans placing him on injured reserve, he will miss a minimum of the following games: ・Week 12: at Jacksonville Jaguars ・Week 13: vs. Washington Commanders ・ Chicago Bears Star Clears Concussion Protocol Ahead of Week 11 vs. New Orleans Saints ・ Los Angeles Chargers Activate Pro Bowler Ahead of Week 10 vs. Baltimore Ravens ・ Minnesota Vikings Lose Key WR for Multiple Weeks After Week 10 Win vs. Green Bay Packers The post Tennessee Titans Place Starter on Injured Reserve Ahead of Week 11 vs. Dallas Cowboys appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

home.headline: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
home.blurb: The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list. Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans. The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game. As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Both teams are in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and both have made major roster changes over the past week. The Colts made several trades ahead of the deadline this past Tuesday, sending veteran players around the league and receiving draft picks in exchange. The Dolphins stood pat at the deadline, but saw quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler, both starters and captains, land on injured reserve. Willis has a groin injury that is expected to keep him out for a few weeks, though season-ending surgery has not been completely ruled out. Sieler ruptured his biceps muscle during the team's Week 9 game against the Detroit Lions, played through the injury for the rest of the contest, but will now require several months of rehab following surgery. Miami enters today with a 1-7 record and is in position to claim the third-overall spot in the 2027 Draft. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and in the top spot for the spring's college prospect selection process while the 1-7 Tennessee Titans are in the second spot. How will Sunday's game play out? Both teams have to adjust to the recent roster changes. Miami knew who they were entering the season as: stripping their roster down, filling it with younger players, and accepting that this season might be tough, but positioning themselves for future success. The Colts came into 2026 looking to compete in the AFC South; after back-to-back 8-9 seasons, Indianapolis was expecting to take a step forward. Instead, everything seems to have gone wrong for the Colts. That all said, Indianapolis now welcomes a Dolphins team with a first-year quarterback making his NFL debut after being a sixth-round pick in 2025 by the Philadelphia Eagles but spending the entire season on the practice squad. There are a lot of obstacles for the Dolphins in this game, and it feels like the Colts will be able to cover the 3.5 points – though it may end up closer than people think if Miami can get their running game established early. Ollie Gordon II rushing yards: 72.5 Over: -113 Under: -113 Miami's offensive system this year was built around the run – first with De'Von Achane and now with Ollie Gordon II serving as the feature back. Gordon is only averaging 57.9 yards per game, but that includes Week 1 with no carries and Week 2 with three attempts for seven yards. Since becoming the starter in Week 4, Gordon is averaging 83 yards per game, which would be seventh in the league. Miami, with a first-time starting quarterback under center today, will rely on Gordon and the running game. The Colts will throw everything they can to stop the rushing attack, but Miami will have to commit to it and find ways to create space for Gordon. He should be able to top 72.5 yards. Kyle McCord passing touchdowns: 0.5 Over : -188 Under: +142 I like the +142 you could get with the under, but one passing touchdown seems plausible, especially if the Colts stack the box to try to stop Gordon. Then again, the Dolphins didn't score a single touchdown last week against the Lions, so Miami could be held without a passing touchdown this week. I still lean toward the Dolphins finding a way to get McCord his first touchdown pass and build his confidence as the starter. picks.headline: Dolphins vs. Colts Expert Picks: NFL.com Backs Indianapolis, SI Leans Toward Miami
picks.blurb: Dolphins vs. Colts Expert Picks: NFL.com Backs Indianapolis, SI Leans Toward Miami - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Five straight losses will do this to a team's reputation. The Indianapolis Colts are small home favorites against a 1-7 Miami Dolphins team starting a quarterback who has never taken a regular-season snap, and a good chunk of the national media still isn't buying them. By our count, 13 of the 22 experts at ESPN, NFL.com and Sports Illustrated picked Indianapolis to win at Lucas Oil Stadium. The other nine went with Kyle McCord, who replaces Malik Willis after the Dolphins put Willis on injured reserve . NFL.com is unanimous on Indianapolis Nov 8, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) makes a catch during the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images All five NFL.com editors picked the Colts , and all five expect a low-scoring game. Jeremy Bergman went 17-16, Brooke Cersosimo 16-13, Gennaro Filice 20-9, Bobby Kownack 10-6 and Dan Parr 20-16. Cersosimo's reasoning had more to do with Miami than with Indianapolis. She wrote that for the Dolphins, "it feels like it's back at square one with McCord under center." ESPN gives the Colts a narrow edge ESPN's panel split 4-3 for Indianapolis . Mike Clay, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody and Jason Reid took the Colts, while Matt Bowen, Dan Graziano and Kalyn Kahler picked Miami. Seth Walder's betting column pointed to McCord's debut as the reason to like the Colts defense to score a touchdown , and that's the kind of game the Colts need. A defense that allows 27.7 points per game rarely gets a quarterback this inexperienced. SI is the outlier Nov 8, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Sports Illustrated's panel went 6-4 for Miami . Albert Breer, Mitch Goldich, Gilberto Manzano, Conor Orr, Matt Verderame and Peter Dewey took the Dolphins. Eva Geitheim, Mike Kadlick, John Pluym and Iain MacMillan stuck with the Colts. It says a lot about the last month in Indianapolis. Daniel Jones has 10 interceptions , Josh Downs and Keenan Allen were traded Tuesday , and Shane Steichen has seen his team give away a lead late, like it did when Dallas came back in the final two minutes last week. Jonathan Taylor is the reason the Colts are still favored. He has 656 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and the Colts turned down second-round offers to keep him. If he gets 25 carries against a 1-7 team, the nine experts who picked Miami will be wrong. away.headline: Dolphins lose a third DL for the season in two weeks
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins lost Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps injury in Week 9 and lost Zeek Biggers to miniscus injury in Week 10, but there's even more devastating news for the team's defensive line depth. According to ESPN's Marcel Louis-Jacques , Dolphins defensive lineman Jordan Phillips tore his biceps on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the rest of the season. Phillips, 22, joined the Dolphins as a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft after a collegiate career split between Tennessee and Maryland. As a rookie, he played 43% of the team's defensive snaps in 17 games and recorded 34 tackles and a quarterback hit. This year, Phillips played 59% of the team's defensive snaps in nine games and recorded 28 tackles and two quarterback hits. With these three injuries, the Dolphins don't have much talent left in the room. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only defensive tackles left on the roster, and Jordan Jefferson is still on the practice squad. Miami will definitely have to bring in outside help before their Week 11 battle with the Buffalo Bills . This article originally appeared on Dolphins Wire: Dolphins lose a third DL for the season in two weeks

away.headline: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries?
away.blurb: That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. Analysis: This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. Jarrett Bell: Colts 26, Dolphins 20 Nick Brinkerhoff: Dolphins 13, Colts 10 Chris Bumb

away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN

Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Miami Dolphins news: Zane Gonzalez waived, Colts game review, and injury updates
away.blurb: Miami has worked out several kickers over the past few weeks, giving them an idea of who is available to replace Gonzalez. Tuesday is typically tryout day in the NFL, and Miami will likely bring in a few kickers to audition before signing someone later in the day. The Splash Zone returns this morning to collect all the latest news, updates, and rumors in one place for you. Check out the collection below: More bad news hits Miami’s trenches as another defensive lineman is ruled out for the remainder of the year. You’ve played it on SB Nation’s website. Now check it out on the SB Nation app! Want to join in the conversation and share your thoughts or point of view on the Dolphins? Check out The Feed , our community-driven discussion about the Dolphins, football, or just about anything on your mind. You can find the feed on the front page of The Phinsider. Jump in now to advance the Dolphins discussion. The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with much of the postgame focus on the two missed field goals and a missed extra point by kicker Zane Gonzalez. Special teams have been inconsistent for much of the 2026 season in Miami, but missing seven points’ worth of kicks in a two-point loss was beyond even the normal inconsistency. On Monday, Miami moved on from Gonzalez, the second kicker they have cut this year. Gonzalez signed with the Dolphins as a free agent during the offseason, with the coaches looking to bring competition to incumbent kicker Riley Patterson. Gonzalez landed on injured reserve at the start of August, however, and was later released in exchange for an injury settlement. Miami began the season with Patterson, but released him in late October, re-signing Gonzalez to the practice squad. After three games as an elevated practice squad member, Gonzalez was added to the Dolphins’ 53-man roster for the Colts game – and now Miami will be looking for their third kicker this year. The waiving of Gonzalez was one part of a busy day for the Dolphins. The news around the team continued to review the Colts game, update injuries, including a season-ending injury to defensive tackle Zeek Biggers, and look at the rookies after 10 weeks. home.headline: Colts place LB on injured reserve, sign WR to 53-man roster
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts announced two more roster moves on Tuesday. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies has been placed on injured reserve, and wide receiver Quez Watkins has been signed from the practice squad to the active roster. Carlies suffered a neck injury against Dallas in Week 9 and did not play last week against Miami. This season, he has played 219 defensive snaps and made five starts. He's recorded three QB pressures, 19 total tackles, and an interception. Carlies will have to miss a minimum of four games on IR. Watkins was signed to the practice squad on Oct. 6. Watkins is a former draft pick, selected in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL draft by the Philadelphia Eagles . Listed at 6-0, 193 pounds, Watkins has appeared in 49 games and made 25 starts. In his career, he's caught 104 passes for 1,304 yards with six touchdowns. The bulk of his snaps have come from the slot, but he has experience lining up outside as well. Watkins was elevated to the game day roster against Miami but did not see any snaps. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: Colts place LB on injured reserve, sign WR to 53-man roster

With both teams looking to turn their seasons around, the Saints will need another strong performance from quarterback Tyler Shough and their defense to secure consecutive victories for the first time this season. Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 21-14 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) makes a catch with Cleveland Browns cornerback Tyson Campbell (7) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season. On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns). The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key. Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility. However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude. Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease. Prediction: Panthers 21, Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 27-21 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough (6) looks to pass against the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places. I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places. Jordyn Tyson should be full speed for the first time this year. Trevor Etienne will be on the field, probably taking it easy at first, the way Tyson did when coming back from a hamstring injury. The offensive line is like a deck of cards, getting shuffled again. The defense doesn't take the ball away, yet it has two of the best pass rushers in the NFL on the same team. The leading rusher is a journeyman running back who just runs downhill all the time The quarterback doesn't have the protection or running game needed, but is rated statistically as one of the best in the league. The offense cannot get going in the first quarter to save its life. On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all. Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much. Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line. Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column. Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants . Is the field goal crap shoot fixed with Charlie Smyth ? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark. There is hope, and I am going with it. Prediction: Saints 27, Panthers 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . Mark Livingston: Saints 24, Panthers 21 The Carolina Panthers have a chance to pick up a much-needed division win against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Zach Roberts: Panthers 24, Saints 23 The margins are as thin as can possibly be this Sunday. These two teams are evenly matched. The Panthers have the best win (over Detroit in Week 4), but the Saints have been better of late (coming off an OT win over the Browns). They are not separated by much. It's almost impossible to predict this one. Will the Saints' strong pass rush make mincemeat of the Panthers' weak offensive line? Will Bryce Young shred the Saints' fifth-worst pass defense? Can Tyler Shough take advantage of a depleted Panthers' secondary? Might Chuba Hubbard plow through the Saints' fourth-worst rushing defense? The Panthers have more advantages than disadvantages, and they could get back a number of healthy contributors. Still, it won't be an easy one. Preston Palm: Panthers 37, Saints 34 If there's ever a time for Carolina to get right, it’s on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. This Saints defense is the second-worst pass defense Carolina has faced. New Orleans ranks 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 236.6 per game. As an overall defense, New Orleans is arguably the worst, ranking 29th in rushing yards allowed per game. Carolina may have reinforcements coming to the defense, as EDGE Jaelan Phillips and cornerback Will Lee III are both listed as questionable for Sunday. Here are our staff picks and predictions for Week 10's grudge match between the New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers . An early lead on the NFC South title is on the line between two teams that just might be the best squads in the NFL's worst division. Getting a win is always important, but it could be crucial as the Saints look to keep their season alive and attack the back half of their schedule. Saints 25, Panthers 24 This should be a close one; we've got an overachieving Panthers team running up against a Saints team that can't figure out how to play with a lead. New Orleans has gotten the better of Bryce Young over the years and they did sweep Carolina last season but we'll have to see if that translates. If the Panthers can take advantage of a beaten-up Saints offensive line (they'll be without Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy and first-round right tackle Taliese Fuaga, with rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright starting at right guard), it'll be a long afternoon for Tyler Shough. We'll guess the return of Travis Etienne Jr. at running back and Jordyn Tyson's emergence at wide receiver makes enough of a difference to win the day. Bold prediction: This game goes to overtime, too, but Tyson comes down with the game-winning score. -- John Sigler Saints 31, Panthers 17 Despite Carolina's lofty ranking against the pass, I love the matchup in favor of the Saints. The right side of the New Orleans line is a huge concern, but I think the Saints can run the ball with some success to their left and set up some play-action shots for Tyler Shough. The Saints just have too many quality pass catchers for the Panthers, and it'll show. On defense, New Orleans has always had great success against Bryce Young. That'll continue on Sunday, with Chase Young and Carl Granderson harassing Bryce all day and hopefully a rebound performance from the New Orleans secondary. The Panthers could have some success on the ground with Chuba Hubbard, but they won't be able to keep pace with the New Orleans offense. Bold prediction: Tyler Shough gets his first 300-yard passing game since opening week, as both Chris Olave and rookie Jordyn Tyson have over 100 receiving yards. -- Bob Rose Panthers 27, Saints 20 The Saints struggle to sustain drives and Olave's big afternoon isn't enough to overcome missed opportunities. Bryce Young makes enough plays to keep Carolina ahead, forcing New Orleans to play catch-up in the second half. The Panthers get a late defensive stop to seal the win and leave the Saints searching for their first stretch of consecutive wins this season. away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress.
