away.headline: Is Travis Etienne Jr. Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Panthers vs. Saints in NFL Week 10)
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. has not played since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury, and he's officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers. The Saints plan to activate RB Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve today, putting him in line to return to action Sunday vs. the Panthers, per source. With Etienne in line to return, I'm targeting him in the prop market against a shaky Carolina run defense. Is Travis Etienne Jr. Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Panthers vs. Saints in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE Etienne is on injured reserve, but it was reported on Saturday that the Saints plan to activate him and play him in Week 10. That's great news for this backfield, as New Orleans is averaging just 3.8 yards per carry as a team and has the fifth-fewest rushing yards in the league through nine weeks. Etienne entered the season as a potential bellcow in this offense after the Saints signed him away from the Jacksonville Jaguars in free agency. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. home.headline: Saints now own the NFL's longest 'Sunday Night Football' drought
home.blurb: It also meant the New Orleans Saints could get flexed into their first Sunday night game in almost five years. With the Chargers-Patriots game flexed out, the Saints' Week 12 road trip to face the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) might have made sense as a replacement. Sure, the Saints are plenty bad themselves (their 3-6 record speaks for itself) but if the NFL wanted to highlight the playoff-ready Bengals, New Orleans might have looked like an appealing punching bag. Years of incompetence have led NBC to freeze the Saints out of prime time ever since they set a SNF record for the fewest points scored -- their 9-0 shutout win over Tom Brady and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was memorable, but it wasn't what TV execs looking for. It's been just over four years and eleven months since that Dec. 20 upset back in 2021, with Week 12's game date (Nov. 29) falling just short of the five-year anniversary. home.headline: Saints could be on their third-string right tackle against the Bears
home.blurb: We’re about to see the outlook for the New Orleans Saints offensive line go from bad to worse. On Monday, head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that the knee injury Asim Richards suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers would knock him out for multiple games. The Saints are about to embark on a two-week road trip for matchups with the playoff-ready Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals , and they might be working with their third-string right tackle. Richards was filling in for Taliese Fuaga on the right side, who went down in practice last week with his own knee injury. If Fuaga still can’t play against Chicago this week, the Saints would likely be starting Mason Murphy, who they claimed off of waivers earlier this summer. Richards had drawn a lot of ire from Saints fans for his mistakes in pass protection (he spent most of the last two months replacing Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle) but Moore set him up for failure. Richards was given even less help from blocking tight ends and chipping running backs than the starters he replaced, and Moore’s refusal to adjust put him in a bad spot. When asked if Fuaga and center Erik McCoy (who also missed the Panthers game, with a biceps injury) could play this week, Moore offered a noncommittal “We’ll see.” Stay tuned. away.headline: Is Garrett Wilson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Bills vs. Jets in NFL Week 10)
away.blurb: Wilson is officially listed as questionable for the AFC East battle with the Buffalo Bills, but he appears to be trending in the right direction to play. Garrett Wilson (concussion) officially listed questionable for Week 10. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson needs to clear one more step to get out of the consussion protocol, but Glenn believes that will happen in time for Sunday's game. Last week, New York scored just 12 points with Wilson out of the lineup, and it slipped to 16th in the league in EPA/Play on offense as a result. This season, Wilson has appeared in eight of the Jets' nine games, catching 43 passes for 527 yards and three scores. He's played 88.5 percent of the team's offensive snaps, so he'll be out there for almost every play against Buffalo if he's able to go. away.headline: Bills starting tackle misses practice as four offensive linemen deal with injuries
away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. Brown was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, when practice participation was estimated. The Bills have four starting offensive linemen on their injury report, including left tackle Dion Dawkins (rib), left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) and center Connor McGovern (neck). All three were limited Wednesday and Thursday. Buffalo also listed cornerback Christian Benford as a limited participant for the second consecutive day because of a wrist injury . Benford injured his right wrist against Minnesota, underwent an X-ray at halftime and returned before leaving again in the third quarter. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, while defensive tackle Greg Gaines (calf) was a full participant both days after missing two consecutive games. Defensive back Sam Franklin Jr . was added to Thursday's injury report with a shoulder injury and was limited. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson was limited for the second consecutive day because of a concussion that forced him to miss Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) did not practice for the second consecutive day. Now four starters are dealing with injuries heading into Sunday's game against the New York Jets. Dawkins and Anderson missed Buffalo's 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Tylan Grable started at left tackle, while Austin Corbett filled in at left guard. Brown returned against Minnesota after missing Buffalo's previous game against Baltimore because of a back injury. The Bills (7-1) visit the Jets (2-7) at 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, at MetLife Stadium. The Jets have multiple several injury concerns. Cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was also absent Thursday because of an illness. Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, including game status designations for Sunday's game.

away.headline: Buffalo Bills roster moves: DB Te'Cory Couch signed to practice squad
away.blurb: The 27-year-old defender out of the University of Miami has played in four games for Buffalo this season. In those games, Couch has made eight tackles (6 solo), showcasing a knack for limiting big plays after the catch with solid tackling. Couch joined the Bills in 2024, entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent. A potential candidate to take over that roster opening is veteran wide receiver Terrell Shavers, whose return-to-practice window was recently opened as the next step toward a return to the field following a devastating knee injury against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the Bills’ 2025 NFL playoff run. The Buffalo Bills announced a series of roster moves as they begin preparations to host the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium for Week 11. Buffalo has signed defensive back Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad, bringing him back to One Bills Drive after being released ahead of last weekend’s game and once he cleared waivers Monday afternoon. To make room for Couch, Buffalo once again parted ways with veteran offensive guard Nick Broeker, who has been re-added to the team’s practice squad several times already this season. Broeker has yet to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills, though he has previously played in 12 games (2023 and 2024 seasons) for the Denver Broncos. Broeker was originally drafted by Buffalo in Round 7 (230th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Bills also announced that rookie offensive guard Ar’maj Reed-Adams has been placed on Injured Reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games. With Reed-Adams heading to IR, that opens up a spot on Buffalo’s 53-man roster.

Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook . While the Seahawks are large favorites, they'll depend on their dominant defense to get the job done yet again as their inconsistent offense is still quite injured. Seattle's "Dark Side" defense will welcome the Raiders' first overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, to the NFL and hope to slow Klint Kubiak's offense, which is averaging 26.4 points per game. Here are four bets/game picks to consider ahead of Sunday's game. 1. Jadarian Price anytime touchdown (+190) While Seattle's rookie running back has battled injuries this season, it's still hard to believe that he's yet to find the end zone. Price has shown the most juice of any Seahawks running back and emerged as a receiving threat last week against the Cardinals. With Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock still hampered by injuries, Price is likely to get a lot of work in the passing and running game against a struggling Raiders defense. Las Vegas' defense has allowed large receiving days to running backs this season, with the worst coming against the Buffalo Bills when back James Cook totaled 58 yards on three catches. While it might be hard to envision betting on the Seahawks offense after they only hung 17 on the Cardinals, a second week with Lock as the leading man should lead to a more complete game plan, allowing them to score and make a statement. 2. Maxx Crosby to record a sack (+144) With Charles Cross out and Abe Lucas struggling this season, there's a near guarantee that the Raiders' star pass rusher will be active in the Seahawks backfield on Sunday. Crosby leads the Raiders with four sacks, and while he hasn't quite been in game-wrecking self this season, he shouldn't need to be to get home against an injured Lock. 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 89.5 receiving yards (-114) Coming off his quietest outing of the year, there's no question that Smith-Njigba should be more involved with the Seahawks offense this week. JSN has totaled over 100 yards in all, but two of his games this season and has padded his total against poor secondaries, which should include Las Vegas' unit. While I already mentioned this in the Price prop, I'll say it again: the Raiders' defense is not good. Las Vegas secondary gives up an average of 234 passing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the league. Even though Lock is still dealing with an injury, JSN should be so open on Sunday he'll only need half an arm to get it to him. 4. Seahawks -6.5 (-110) Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald is undefeated against quarterbacks making their first start, and there's no reason this game should be different. Mendoza has limited reps as a starter and is getting thrown to the wolves against a Seahawks defense that is riding high after holding an NFC West rival to just three points last week. Lock and the Seahawks' offense may struggle early, but there is simply too much star power for the Raiders defense to handle. Las Vegas' defense has thrived on turnovers, so Seattle will need another turnover-free game from Lock and Price like they got last week. If the Seahawks' offense can stay clean there's no doubt the defense will handle Mendoza and allow the Seahawks to handle the Raiders with ease. While the Seahawks are optimistic about Lock's availability, Darnold has already been ruled out for Sunday's November 15 game against Las Vegas. Darnold is recovering from quadriceps and rib injuries that also kept him out of Seattle's Week 9 victory over Arizona. Seattle has a Week 11 bye following its matchup against Las Vegas, giving Darnold additional time to recover before the Seahawks return to action against the San Francisco 49ers on November 29. Macdonald indicated Monday that Darnold has a chance to return following the bye, although no specific return date has been established. They'll also take on an Arizona Cardinals team that upset them in Week 6. A win would help the Rams keep pace for the Wild Card as well as deliver the team's first divisional win in 2026. It'll be an interesting showdown given how well the Rams defense performed in Week 9 with Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett finally on the field together, especially given they'll take on rookie quarterback Carson Beck and a similarly-injured Cardinals offense. They also remember what happened the last time these two met. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16 at SoFi Stadium in Week 6. That game was played with Puka Nacua. This one won't be, since he and Davante Adams are both on injured reserve. Arizona is starting rookie Carson Beck in his NFL debut, and nobody we found thinks that's a fair fight. None of them has Los Angeles scoring more than 25. Cersosimo called them "big road favorites in the desert" and pointed to Myles Garrett, who had three sacks and a forced fumble in his return against Washington. Garrett is questionable with a knee issue, though Sean McVay said Friday he expects him to play . "He's feeling good," McVay said. "It's more of just getting him feeling as good as possible." ESPN and SI agree ESPN's Pamela Maldonado (23-16), Eric Moody (27-17) and Aaron Schatz (27-20) all took the Rams, and ESPN's FPI gives Los Angeles an 87.4% chance to win. Sports Illustrated's 10-person panel, including Albert Breer and Conor Orr, went 10-for-10 on the Rams . Bleacher Report was just as sure. All seven of its NFL writers took the Rams to cover , and Maurice Moton expects them to bracket Trey McBride and wear down Arizona's front to avenge that loss. Average the five NFL.com scores and the Rams win by 9.6 points. FPI projects 11.5. Set those next to the two-point game Arizona won in October, and the gap shows how much the experts think has changed in four weeks. The case for the Cardinals is the October game itself. Arizona held the Rams to 16 points with Nacua on the field, and Matthew Stafford has little left to throw to now. A rookie quarterback who protects the ball can keep a game like this one close for a long time. We still picked the Rams in this one when we went through the rest of their schedule, and Arizona is 0-3 at home. home.headline: NFL injury news: Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew suffers torn UCL, set for season ending surgery | Report
home.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
home.blurb: India, Nov. 15 -- Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing elbow. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported on November 15 that Minshew is planning to have the surgery, although he is still working on the timing of the procedure. The injury is a major setback for the Cardinals, who have already placed the veteran quarterback on Injured Reserve. Minshew's 2026 campaign is officially over, leaving rookie Carson Beck to take charge of Arizona's quarterback room. Gardner Minshew To Undergo Surgery After Torn UCL Injury According to Schefter, Minshew is expected to undergo surgery to address the torn UCL in his right elbow. While the quarterback has not finalised when he will have the procedure, he is planning to go ahead with the operation. The injury occurred during Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on November 8. Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit Minshew during his throwing motion on the final play of the first half, forcing a fumble. Minshew immediately appeared to be in discomfort but surprisingly returned after halftime and completed the game. He finished the contest with 21 completions on 30 attempts for 166 passing yards. However, the Cardinals suffered a 17-3 defeat against Seattle. Cardinals Place Gardner Minshew On Injured Reserve The Arizona Cardinals officially placed Minshew on Injured Reserve on November 10, confirming that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before suffering the injury, Minshew had completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns across two appearances for Arizona. His brief stint with the Cardinals included an impressive performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Coming off the bench, Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, helping Arizona secure a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory. His performance earned him the starting quarterback position, but his promotion was followed by the devastating elbow injury. Carson Beck Takes Over As Cardinals Starting Quarterback With Minshew sidelined, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to lead the Cardinals' offence. Arizona has also strengthened its quarterback depth by signing veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. Johnson joined from the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, while Aguilar arrived from the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad. The Cardinals are now relying on their rookie quarterback to navigate the remainder of a challenging season. Minshew's injury also creates uncertainty surrounding his future in Arizona, as the veteran quarterback is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 campaign. For now, the priority will be his recovery following surgery as the Cardinals look to move forward without their experienced signal caller.

picks.blurb: Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images | Getty Images Mike Poland · SB Nation Sun, November 15, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys return home at 4-5 after escaping the Indianapolis Colts with a nail-biting victory, but the difficulty level rises considerably this week. The San Francisco 49ers are at 7-1 and own the best record in the NFC. Dallas showed against the Colts that its offense can move the football against anybody, but beating San Francisco will require a much cleaner performance, and scoring touchdowns rather than settling for field goals, or worse, falling victim to turnovers. When San Francisco has the ball Everything starts with Christian McCaffrey. San Francisco does not need him to simply line up and run between the tackles, Kyle Shanahan moves him around, gets him involved in the passing game and uses his presence to create space for everyone else. McCaffrey already has nine rushing touchdowns, while Brock Purdy has thrown 17 touchdowns against only five interceptions and ranks among the NFL's most efficient quarterbacks. San Francisco also leads the league in red-zone touchdown rate at an incredible 84%, so Dallas cannot rely on tightening up once the 49ers get close to the goal line. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should take confidence from what it produced in Indianapolis. The Cowboys gained 508 total yards, with Dak Prescott throwing for 335, CeeDee Lamb producing 195 receiving yards and Javonte Williams topping 100 yards rushing. The problem was everything around those numbers. Dallas committed 14 penalties and lost two fumbles, turning what should have been a comfortable win into another game that required Prescott to rescue them in the final minutes. The good news is San Francisco's defense can be attacked. Despite all the talent in its front seven, the 49ers have only 15 sacks, ranking 28th in the NFL. Nick Bosa and recently acquired DeForest Buckner make the defensive line much more dangerous than that number suggests, but Dallas should still give Prescott opportunities to attack downfield. Lamb is now up to 904 receiving yards and is coming off one of his best games of the season. San Francisco also began the week with injuries to their starting cornerbacks and their game status is questionable. If either is missing or limited, Lamb becomes the obvious place for Dallas to attack. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-5) I just don't see the Cowboys being that competitive against one of the Super Bowl favorites. In a matchup of organizational dysfunction and well oiled machine, I'll sadly pick the 49ers to win 31-16. Brandon Loree (6-3) At this point, it's probably the Cowboys' toughest challenge and, unfortunately, their biggest thorn in the side since 2021. The 49ers are way better in almost every category compared to Dallas despite having similar if not worse, injury luck. If the Cowboys can somehow pull a rabbit out of their hat and win this game, get ready to hear some outrageous playoff talk. Seeing is believing, so I'll have to see it happen in order to believe—Dallas loses at home 33-23. Dyllan Rivers (5-4) Sometimes the NFL makes absolutely no sense. Teams that have no business winning will go out and upset the heavy favorite. But this is not one of those weeks. Christian McCaffrey goes crazy and Dallas falls to the 49ers 37-27. Matt Holleran (4-5) Until I see it happen I refuse to believe the Cowboys will beat a Kyle Shanahan-lead 49ers team. Dallas does not win back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer and I would be absolutely shocked if they did just that against a San Francisco team that just may be the best in the league. I hope I'm wrong, but I don't see this one being close. Give me the 49ers in a rout, 37-17. Mike Poland (4-5) An entire panel going for the 49ers to win this one, and my head says the Cowboys lose this week to a strong San Francisco roster. But I'll break the clean sweep here so any optimistic Cowboys fans here on BTB have something to align with on the staff predictions. A very tentative and nervous score prediction here where Dallas wins 28-21. And I'm willing to take the hit on this one. Put your prediction in the comments before the game begins.

picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. home.headline: When will Jake Ferguson come back to the Cowboys?
home.blurb: One week after surviving the Indianapolis Colts in a thriller, the Dallas Cowboys ' hopes of winning the middling NFC East are still very much alive. But with a 4-5 record, they don't exactly have much margin for error. This Dallas team can't afford any more inexplicable or unacceptable losses, of which it has already suffered more than its fair share this season. It's time to start building some momentum or risk losing a golden opportunity at a division title. With a home matchup against the heavyweight San Francisco 49ers on deck on Sunday, Dallas will have to soldier on without its starting tight end. Woof. It's not an ideal situation, to say the least! Fifth-year NFL veteran Jake Ferguson is missing the 49ers game with knee and ankle injuries. It won't be the only game Ferguson misses with the injuries, either. A brutal turn of events for Dallas: Multiple weeks could mean anything in the context of an NFL injury. Given how many lingering lower-body injuries Ferguson has, let's assume the Cowboys really let him rest up and give him at least three games off to recover. That would mean we probably won't see Ferguson play again until a Monday night game against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, December 7th. That could be the smartest play if the Cowboys want the best version of Ferguson for a stretch run featuring pivotal games against fellow NFC East contenders in the New York Giants and the Washington Commanders . We'll see how the Cowboys fare without their starting tight end for a little while. This article originally appeared on For The Win: When will Jake Ferguson come back to the Cowboys?

Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup Imagn Images In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers . Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley . Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season. Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Chargers live Date: Monday, Nov. 16 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Ravens -4.5, O/U 38.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Chargers have the ball The Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes. Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston , Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options. Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton , Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry. Other than all that, though, things are going really well! That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change. When the Ravens have the ball It's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago. We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling. We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson , but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns . The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers , and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here. Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside. Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry , so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle. Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season. The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews . I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. After all that, the Bolts have the same team heading into Week 10 when they face the Ravens . Los Angeles is the league's only winless team. Daiyan Henley records a season-high in tackles It was a whirlwind of a week for the Chargers linebacker. First, Henley finds out he was traded from the team that drafted him four seasons ago to their division rival, the Broncos. And a little over 24 hours later, the trade fell through after a failed physical. Henley is back with the team now, and I think he will be out for blood. Last week, Henley recorded a season-high 10 tackles against the Texans . I think he set another season-high in primetime against the Ravens. Chargers keep Derrick Henry under 100 rushing yards The Chargers' run defense ranks in the bottom half in that category, allowing an average of 122 rushing yards per game. Through eight games, the Chargers have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns. Los Angeles will face their toughest test yet with running back Derrick Henry. It's been tough sledding for Henry over the past few weeks, and I think that trend continues. Henry has rushed for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. C hargers force three turnovers The Ravens will have yet another quarterback under center: veteran Jacoby Brissett. The Chargers' defense has been the team's only bright spot. Their offense and defense haven't provided enough complementary football this season, but forcing turnovers could help change that. Brissett has had a mixed -to-rough time taking care of the football this season. Los Angeles will take care of that. Justin Herbert has his best game of the season on primetime Justin Herbert is playing the worst football of his NFL career. He's coming off another disappointing performance against Houston, throwing for 193 yards and one touchdown in a 44-22 loss. However, Herbert has a chance to play his best game yet against an inconsistent Ravens defense. Baltimore is allowing 329.7 passing yards per game, and while Herbert has yet to reach 300+ passing yards, that will happen in front of a national audience. Credit: AP/Stephanie Scarbrough OWINGS MILLS, Md. — Lamar Jackson's thumb injury was expected to weaken the Baltimore Ravens — but not this much. There's now mounting evidence that the Jackson-less Ravens might be one of the worst teams in the NFL after Monday night's 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore has lost five straight, and the Ravens haven't even had a lead in any of the last 13 quarters. Against a Los Angeles team that had dropped 11 in a row, Baltimore — the franchise of Ray Lewis, Jonathan Ogden and Ed Reed — was pushed around. “The standard’s been what it is around here since ’96, and right now we are disgracing those standards,” safety Kyle Hamilton said. “As leaders, as players and as a team. Whatever flak we get is warranted.” The Ravens were held to 16 yards rushing, their lowest total in 10 years. At halftime, Baltimore had run six times for 0 yards. “Unacceptable, honestly,” coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “The first half, to have no yards rushing, it’s embarrassing. And so, we’ll keep trying to find a better way to do it.” Derrick Henry's frustration afterward was understandable. “I don’t mean to be rude, but you all are asking questions I think you all know the answer to,” he said. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. home.headline: Justin Herbert Avoids Injury After Low Hit in Win Against the Ravens
home.blurb: In a less-than-marquee primetime game at the Baltimore Ravens, the Chargers were able to squeeze out a 23-20 win. They did so mostly on the back of Omarion Hampton, who rushed for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. The NFL’s review of the play could take some time, and likely will not come down with a decision until next week. That is if the hit meets the criteria, which is questionable. Green hit Herbert below the waist but had his helmet above the knees. Entering NFL Week 10, the Los Angeles Chargers had not won a single game. They were 0-8, had a point differential of -98 and were in the No. 1 spot for next year’s draft. On Monday Night Football, the team finally snatched a win. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has had quite the rough season, although did not look too shabby on MNF. He was 12-for-18 for 129 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions with an 87.5 passer rating. With Los Angeles leading 20-13 with time winding down in the third quarter, Herbert was hit low on a pass attempt by Baltimore linebacker Mike Green. The play drew a roughing the passer penalty, and was posted on X by Rate the Refs. That call was on the first play of the drive, and the Chargers were able to take advantage. They got into the red zone and gave kicker Cameron Dicker a 35-yard chip shot field goal, which he nailed. Herbert was just fine after taking the low hit, and Green as well, but there may be a fine coming the latter’s way. The NFL has notably cracked down on how defenders can hit the quarterback, this being one of additions. Green is in his second season in the league and has never been fined through 27 career games. The standard roughing the passer fine for a first-time offender is $17,911. With Baltimore star QB Lamar Jackson done for the year and the Chargers being 1-8, both teams are looking ahead to the offseason. It has been a disappointing year for both clubs.
